ai_answer: Systematic desensitization (developed by Wolpe) involves three key steps: (1) Training in deep muscle relaxation techniques, (2) Construction of an anxiety hierarchy from least to most anxiety-provoking stimuli, and (3) Gradual pairing of relaxation with increasingly anxiety-provoking imagery/stimuli (counterconditioning). The core principle is reciprocal inhibition—anxiety and relaxation are mutually exclusive states. Hypnosis may not align with these principles because: (1) It relies on suggestion rather than learned self-regulation skills; (2) The relaxation achieved through hypnosis is externally induced rather than self-generated, potentially limiting generalization; (3) Clients may not develop autonomous coping skills; (4) The altered state of consciousness in hypnosis differs from the alert relaxation state in progressive muscle relaxation; (5) Transfer of training to real-world situations may be compromised when relaxation depends on hypnotic induction.
